the control by diffusion, membrane transport, and changes in the spatial cell size, all add up to the control by chemical reactions and membrane reactions.

the diffusion, the membrane transport and the spatial size of the cell all contribute to the control of cellular reaction networks, and that the sum of the diffusion and membrane transport coefficients is always one and the sum is zero.
the spatial control coefficients are additive for the control of fluxes and intermediate protein concentrations in a spatially heterogeneous reaction network.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the control over the cellular reaction network is a result of a balance between the control coefficients associated with the processes of chemical reactions, membrane transport, diffusion and changes in the spatial cell size.
the spatial control is not negligible in small cells and the diffusion control dominates in larger cells.
the spatial control of cellular reaction networks is governed by the diffusion, transport and spatial size of the system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the control summation theorem is a generalization of the MCA to spatially heterogeneous reaction systems, while the novel summation theorem is a new tool that can be used to quantify the influence of the spatial size of the system on its function.
the control of spatially heterogeneous reaction network can be described by the same control summation theores that are known for the control of homogeneous systems.
the control over the system variables is shared between the spatially separated reaction processes and the spatial size of the cell.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spatial control of cellular reaction networks is a novel and important concept.
the classical MCA is not a universal tool for control analysis, but rather it should be viewed as a particular case of a more general framework.

the control over the cellular reaction network cannot be reduced to the control over the reaction fluxes and concentrations alone, but must also take the control over the spatial size of the cell into account.
